cornerCallouts: The cars are flying down the start/finish straight, preparing to brake hard for Turn 1, the first chicane.
Drivers need to carry as much speed as possible through Turn 2, the right-hander, to set themselves up for the next section.
Turn 3 is a crucial corner, a tight left-hander where precision and balance are key to maintaining momentum.
Through Turn 4, a tricky right-hand kink that requires commitment and a steady hand on the wheel.
Onto Turns 5 and 6, a fast left-right flick that demands quick reflexes and accurate placement of the car.
Drivers need to be careful on exit of Turn 7, the left hander, as it's easy to run wide and lose time.
Turn 8 is a long right-hander, requiring sustained g-forces and a well-balanced car to maintain speed.
The final two corners, Turns 9 and 10, are crucial for setting up an overtaking opportunity on the final straight.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor in this Sprint race. Managing the tires through the fast corners will be crucial.
With a relatively short pit lane, the pit stop loss time is minimized, making multiple stops a viable option.
Fuel consumption will be less of a concern on this shorter Sprint layout, allowing drivers to push harder for longer.
The pit window will likely open relatively early, with teams looking to undercut their rivals.
The Nürburgring's abrasive surface can take its toll on the tires, so teams will need to monitor wear closely.
A well-timed safety car could completely change the complexion of the race, so teams need to be ready to react quickly.
Overcut or undercut? Strategy teams will be burning the midnight oil to see which provides an advantage on this circuit.
Track position is key here at the Nürburgring Sprint layout, with limited overtaking opportunities. A good start is crucial.
